chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abi Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a mukatab who killed a man by mistake. He said:

If his master, when he made the contract of mukatabah with him, stipulated against him that if he became unable, then he would be returned to slavery, then he is in the position of owned slaves: he is handed over to the heirs of the slain; if they wish, they may kill him, and if they wish, they may sell him. But if his master, when he made the contract of mukatabah with him, did not stipulate that against him, and he had already paid something of his mukatabah, then Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali عليه السلام used to say: 'The mukatab is freed in proportion to what he has paid of his mukatabah.' And it is upon the Imam to pay to the heirs of the slain from the blood-money in proportion to the amount of the mukatab that has been freed. And the blood of a Muslim man is not to be lost. And I hold that whatever remains upon the mukatab from what he has not yet paid belongs to the heirs of the slain: they may employ him for his lifetime in proportion to what remains upon him, but they do not have the right to sell him.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: The legal heirs of the person who was killed
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: Blood-money; financial compensation due for unlawful killing
key_terms.الرِّقِّ: The state of slavery or bondage
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: The Imam, who here bears legal authority and public responsibility
key_terms.خَطَأً: Unintentionally; by mistake, without deliberate intent to kill
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave under a manumission contract who purchases his freedom through agreed payments
key_terms.يُعْتَقُ: He is set free; manumission applies in proportion to payment made

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a mukatab who kills a person by mistake in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal ruling for a mukatab slave who kills someone by mistake, distinguishing between cases where the master had stipulated reversion to slavery and cases where no such stipulation existed. It also affirms that any partial freedom already earned by payment is recognized, and that the Imam bears responsibility for paying the corresponding portion of the diyah so that the blood of a Muslim is not left uncompensated.
